business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Swiss Confederation (Schweizerische Eidgenossenschaft / Confédération suisse / Confederazione Svizzera)
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (Federal State; cantonal seat of the Aktiengesellschaft, e.g., Zug, Zurich, or Geneva, determines the registering Commercial Register Office)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic; Swiss Code of Obligations - OR/CO, SR 220; federal statutes and ordinances; cantonal procedural rules for register appeals)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EFTA Convention (Vaduz revision 2013, in force 1 June 2014)
EFTA-China Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 July 2014) - relevant for Chinese-source or Chinese-destination used machinery flows
Switzerland-China BIT (signed 27 January 2009, in force 6 November 2009) - applicable if a Chinese UBO or parent is present
Swiss DTAA network exceeding 100 jurisdictions (OECD Model-based, with MLI positions effective 1 January 2020)
EU-Switzerland bilateral sectoral agreements (free movement of persons, mutual recognition, customs facilitation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG), SR 955.0 of 10 October 1997, as revised with effect from 1 January 2023; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Arts. 627 no. 5, 697j-697m (UBO identification and declaration) and Art. 954 (advance registration of firm name); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411) Arts. 1, 46-51; Commercial Register Fees Ordinance (SR 221.411.2); Federal Act on the Implementation of International Sanctions (Embargo Act, SR 946.231); FINMA Circular 2020/1 (PEP and sanctions, applied analogously by onboarding banks); Swissness Act and Coats of Arms Protection Act (SR 232.21) for name elements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial copy of valid passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of origin / residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961; Switzerland a member state since 11 February 1973) - or consular legalization if the origin state is not a Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / Certificate of Good Conduct of each UBO and each Swiss resident director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national or cantonal police authority of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) of each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, register excerpt and UBO certificate (with ownership chart) of any corporate UBO or holding parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the corporate UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Swiss notarial Power of Attorney (Vollmacht) for the Swiss incorporation agent, countersigned by each UBO before a recognized authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction, then certified by the Swiss cantonal notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by acceptance by the Swiss Commercial Register

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and material counterparties (sellers, LC issuing banks, consignees) against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) SECO sanctions list and Swiss autonomous measures under the Embargo Act, including sectoral measures aligned with EU restrictive measures for Russia/Belarus; (iii) OFAC SDN List and the 50% ownership rule, applied whenever settlement occurs in USD via correspondent banking; (iv) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List as best-practice benchmark; (v) PEP status review per FINMA Circular 2020/1, capturing politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates. Additional trade-compliance screening is required because used hydraulic excavators may be dual-use relevant (EU/CH Dual-Use Regulation Annex I; ECCN 2A002/2B001 as applicable): destination country, end-use and red-flag indicators (transshipment havens, shell freight forwarders, cash-equivalent payments) must be analyzed before accepting any order. Continuous monitoring applies from the 90-day pre-incorporation window through the active life of the SWIFT LC and wire-transfer payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Index of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register (zefix.ch); substantive name examination and filing through the cantonal Commercial Register Office (e.g., Handelsregisteramt of the canton of seat) using the Federal e-register platform (e-register.ch)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered firm must be in German, French, Italian, or Romansh; an English-only name is admitted only where clearly non-misleading and accepted by the cantonal office. The name must contain the legal-form marker 'AG', 'SA', or 'Ltd.' in full or abbreviated form (Art. 950-951 OR) and must not be misleading, create likelihood of confusion with existing registered firms or protected trademarks, or suggest activities not actually carried out. Non-Latin-script UBO names are transliterated into the chosen Swiss official language; certified translations of foreign documents are filed as attachments.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Suisse / Schweiz / Helvetia / Svizzera - requires prior written authorization of the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) under the Swissness provisions
Bank / Banque / Banca - requires a banking license under Article 1 of the Swiss Banking Act
Versicherung / Assurances / Insurance - requires FINMA authorization
Federal / Eidgenossenschaft / Confederation / Bund / national coats of arms - requires consent under the Coats of Arms Protection Act
Trust / Fiduciary / Anlagestiftung - requires regulatory assessment where fiduciary or collective-investment activity is implied
Geographic names (e.g., Zug, Geneva, Crypto Valley) - permitted only if the company has a genuine registered seat in that location and the use is not misleading
Terms implying public authority, certification, or charitable status (e.g., Swiss, Helvetia, Foundation) when the company is purely commercial
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal Commercial Register Office refuses the proposed firm (Art. 954 OR), the applicant may within 30 days of notification file a written appeal with the cantonal supervisory authority for the commercial register (Art. 46-51 HRegV). The appeal must specify the requested name, the legal grounds, and proposed corrections; the supervisory authority may replace the name if the conflict is curable (e.g., adding a distinguishing element or changing the canton of seat). A further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) and ultimately to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. The 90-day name assurance may be renewed once for a further 90 days upon payment of the renewal fee; failure to complete incorporation within the extended window forfeits priority as against later applicants.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-agent address is tolerated for the registered seat of an AG provided there is a physical Swiss address for official service of process, mail handling, and retention of corporate books, and provided at least one member of the board of directors authorized to represent the company is resident in Switzerland (Art. 708 para. 1 OR, as revised by the 2023 corporate law reform). For the used-construction-excavator trading model, the tax and customs authorities and the onboarding bank will apply a commercial-substance test (effective place of management; circular doctrine); the AG should maintain real administrative substance in Switzerland, including a physical office, local books, and resident management, to avoid reclassification as a purely letterbox company and consequent treaty-shopping or customs-license risks.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate (estimated 10-15% at pre-incorporation; rising to approximately 25% after bank account opening and on first export declaration). The Commercial Register does not routinely conduct on-site visits, but the onboarding Swiss bank under the medium-risk-enhanced AML tier may require a physical substance visit or documentary verification, and Swiss customs or SECO may initiate desk-based or on-site reviews if the company repeatedly exports used dual-use-relevant earthmoving machinery to high-risk destinations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the deed of incorporation (Statuten) and public deed in the presence of a Swiss notary, including UBO declaration attachment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal notary public (tariff varies by canton; Zug and Zurich benchmark)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff ordinance (statutory scale for a corporation with nominal capital of CHF 100,000); market benchmark CHF 1,500-2,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Advance name clearance and name reservation (Voranmeldung / Zusicherung der Firma, Art. 954 OR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per cantonal register tariff; CHF 100 flat

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Constitutive registration of the AG in the Commercial Register (Handelsregistereintrag)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal Commercial Register Fees Ordinance (SR 221.411.2); CHF 500-700 depending on canton and e-filing mode

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC)
Apostille certification of the UBO and director document bundle (3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Federal Chancellery or cantonal stamping office (for foreign-origin documents: apostille authority of the origin state)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention statutory fee; CHF 30 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of statutes, UBO declarations and foreign registry excerpts into the chosen official Swiss language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted by the canton
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 150-300 per page bundle; sworn-translator tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Blocked capital deposit and bank capital-confirmation certificate (required to prove payment of the minimum subscribed capital of CHF 100,000, with at least CHF 50,000 paid up)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss bank (e.g., UBS, ZKB, Zuger Kantonalbank, or private bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for opening a blocked client account and issuing the capital confirmation (BRV); CHF 300-500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enhanced Due Diligence KYC screening of UBOs, directors and counterparties against PEP, SECO, UN, OFAC, and EU sanctions lists via commercial database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML/KYC data vendor (e.g., Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription/per-case EDD fee; CHF 300-400 per entity set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Trade-compliance red-flag review of the used excavation machinery trade (dual-use ECCN analysis, sensitive destinations, end-use certification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External trade-compliance counsel (Swiss/EU export control lawyer)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for fixed-scope export-control assessment; CHF 600-800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office and corporate-formation agent fee (mail handling, statutory register maintenance, liaison with register office) for the incorporation phase
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss fiduciary or corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for pre-incorporation agent services; CHF 250-400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency and disbursements (courier of apostilled documents, certified copies, registry archive extracts, notary incidentals)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht/OR), Art. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), including Art. 621/626 (minimum capital), Art. 632 (paid-up capital), Art. 716a (inalienable powers of the board), Art. 718 (binding capacity), and Art. 640/641 (shares).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the seat canton, under federal supervision of the Swiss Commercial Register (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of incorporation executed by notarial act, together with the Articles of Association (Statuten) and the application for entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Handelsregistereintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The AG must have minimum share capital of CHF 100,000, at least CHF 50,000 fully paid up before incorporation. The paid-up amount must be deposited into a bank blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company; the bank releases funds only after the Commercial Register excerpt is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the inaugural meeting of the incorporators and the first board, it was unanimously RESOLVED that: (1) the Company’s share capital is fixed at CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 par value each, fully subscribed and paid into a restricted escrow account; (2) the Company’s registered office is adopted at the address in [Canton Zug, Switzerland] and such statutory seat is approved; (3) the following officers are appointed: [X] as Chairman, [Y] as CEO, [Z] as independent board member; (4) the board and the delegated officer are authorized to execute the commercial register filing, open bank accounts, obtain UID, and engage the statutory auditor; (5) the foregoing resolutions take immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Deed of Incorporation and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public admitted in the court of the seat canton; pre-statutory check by Cantonal Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble incorporators before the notary. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, and capital structure. The deed of incorporation and articles of association are executed in the notary's presence, authenticated, and signed. The notary records the par value, paid-up capital, and board members, then issues the notarial public deed (öffentliche Beurkundung).
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of each incorporator
Proof of source of funds for deposit
Certificate of good standing for corporate shareholders (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary rejects the deed due to flawed corporate purpose or capital computation, amend the documents and re-execute before the same notary; if shareholder AML documentation is incomplete, provide bank references or apostilled certificates to satisfy the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (e.g., in Zurich or Zug) offering Sperrkonto and escrow release instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account in the name of the future company. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 for the minimum paid-up requirement (full CHF 100,000 recommended) into this account. Instruct the bank to issue a blocking confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) addressed to the Commercial Register Office; funds are released only after the incorporation excerpt is presented.
required_dossiers: Bank account application in company name
List of shareholders with names and percentages
Statutory declaration on source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions source of wealth, supply bank statements or audited sales contracts; if any shareholder payment is delayed, replace with certified bank draft and obtain an updated blocking confirmation before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application for registration, including the notarized deed, articles, blocking confirmation, and board list, through the e-Coprus system or in person. The registrar conducts a legal vetting of name, seat, capital, and authorized officers. Upon acceptance, the company receives the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and commercial register number.
required_dossiers: List of directors and authorized signatories
Consent of each director to appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency notice (Mängelrüge) is issued, remedy the specified defect within 10 days (e.g., amend purpose clause, correct capital evidence) and resubmit to the same registrar; repeated deficiencies can be cured by requesting a preliminary ruling before final entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB / Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt) via the Commercial Register Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Commercial Register Office transmits the registration data to SHAB for mandatory publication. The SHAB notice contains the company's name, seat, purpose, share capital, board structure, and signature rights. Legal personality is acquired retroactively at the moment of entry in the register, and third-party protections apply after publication.
required_dossiers: SHAB online publication request (if manual filing is needed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SHAB publication is delayed or contains errors, request a corrigendum from the Commercial Register Office; if the company is affected by inaccurate publication, conservatory remedies are resolved through the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Social Security Set-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Cantonal Tax Office, Cantonal Compensation Office (AHV/AVS), and SUVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After UID issuance, file VAT registration with ESTV if annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or opt for voluntary registration. Register for cantonal profit/capital tax and withholding tax, if applicable. Register as an employer with the cantonal compensation office and obtain an employer number; enroll staff in statutory accident insurance (SUVA) and pension schemes.
required_dossiers: Information on business premises and warehouse sites
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed, apply directly to ESTV with UID and regularization; if social security authorities flag non-registration, file retroactively with proof of immediate registration and pay any procedural surcharges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/OFEV) and the cantonal building/fire authorities; no separate industrial trade license applies to wholesale reselling of used machinery
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required by federal or cantonal industrial laws; only municipal/occupational compliances as set out in the environmental and civil defence sections

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU / Office fédéral de l'environnement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA under Annex 1 of the Swiss EIA Ordinance (EUV/IE) for pure trading activities without modification, salvage, or solvent use; any separate storage or maintenance site requires a cantonal environmental preliminary assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliant with Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV): wastewater purity requiring oil separator effluents ≤20 mg/l hydrocarbons; Air Pollution Control Ordinance (LRV/OACI) VOC thresholds for solvent-based maintenance activities; waste management under Ordinance on Avoiding and Disposal of Waste (VVEA) for spent oils, filters, and machinery parts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local Feuerpolizei for storage or display areas, covering escape routes and extinguishing equipment; structural load verification for floors and racking; workplace safety inspection compliant with Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and SUVA occupational hazard directives, including hydraulic cylinder pressurization and noise mitigation controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Hauptabteilung für Mehrwertsteuer; official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; online e-services portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch/e-service
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG/SA) obtains a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) from the cantonal Commercial Register Office upon incorporation; the UID is then activated by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration for VAT purposes and serves as the MWST/TVA number. Foreign enterprises not established in Switzerland but conducting taxable supplies in Switzerland must appoint a Swiss VAT tax representative jointly and severally liable under Art. 97(5) MWSTG, submit the official VAT registration form (application to ESTV), receive a UID/MWST-Nr, and file quarterly or semi-annual VAT returns. Registration is mandatory once taxable worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year excluding VAT; voluntary registration is available to non-established foreign entities for cost-recovery purposes only where the volume of Swiss-source supplies does not exceed the threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (an Aktiengesellschaft is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Swiss federal, cantonal and communal income taxes on its net profits; shareholders are separately taxed on dividends and capital gains; no pass-through or check-the-box treatment is recognised in Swiss tax law)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election and no general hybrid-mismatch election is available. Available Swiss statutory tax elections include: VAT small-business exception waiver election (Art. 13(2) MWSTG); VAT group taxation election for closely controlled Swiss companies (Art. 11 MWSTG); simplified saldo taxation of VAT input/output balances (Art. 37 MWSTG); election between effective rendering of accounts and total-saldo flat rates for transport and certain trades; and, for direct tax purposes, specific deductions such as participation relief and notional-interest-deduction provisions under cantonal tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / imposta sul valore aggiunto) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (MWSTG / LTVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual net worldwide turnover from taxable supplies (excluding VAT), unless explicitly exempt under MWSTG; suppliers below threshold may waive exemption and register voluntarily
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital-stamping or continuous-transaction-control regime. B2B and B2C invoicing by Swiss VAT-registered businesses must contain the statutory VAT invoice particulars (Art. 26 MWSTG); QR-billing (QR-Rechnung) is the standard structured payment instrument for CHF invoices; electronic data interchange formats such as Swiss e-invoicing standards (Swico/SEDEX, FACITO) are permitted but not compulsory. No API-based government clearance is currently required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exported used construction excavators is available under Art. 18(1)(a)-(c) MWSTG where the AG supplies movable physical goods and transports or arranges transport so that the goods are physically removed from Switzerland and delivered to a foreign recipient abroad, and the goods are not used or consumed in Switzerland. Services directly connected with the exported goods (e.g., warranty or repair services performed abroad by a foreign subcontractor) may qualify under Art. 19(1) MWSTG where the service recipient is domiciled abroad and the service is not effectively used in Switzerland. The exporter must substantiate the export with documentary evidence, obtainable by the customs declaration release and by confirming delivery abroad; export invoices must state that the supply is zero-rated under the Swiss VAT Act and must show the recipient's foreign address.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (NCTS customs declaration and/or ATS-ch-Overlay proof of exit from the Swiss customs territory)
Bill of Lading, sea waybill, CMR consignment note or air waybill evidencing physical delivery to a foreign destination

Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT credit evidence confirming that the purchase price was remitted from the foreign buyer's account; where irrevocable letter of credit (LC) is used, the LC and settlement statement are also required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export treatment is subject to retrospective audit by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, which can reassess the supply at 8.1% Swiss VAT plus default interest if the exporter cannot produce complete export-proof documentation within the statutory ten-year retention period. Intentional or deliberate understatement of VAT or false export documentation constitutes tax evasion (Art. 186 MWSTG) and is punishable by a fine of up to three times the tax evaded, plus any imposed ancillary tax penalties; negligent violation attracts fines and interest under Arts. 173 and 175 MWSTG. Customs export misdeclarations may trigger separate Swiss customs penalties and confiscation measures. In practice, for commodity trades such as used construction excavators, export documentation and price repatriation should be completed within 180 days from export declaration to mitigate heightened AML compliance scrutiny and to preserve the zero-rating evidentiary record.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; German: Schweizerische Nationalbank; French: Banque nationale suisse) as the central bank and monetary authority of the Swiss Confederation, acting alongside the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking conduct and AML supervision, and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for international sanctions and export controls. Switzerland maintains no separate foreign exchange administration; the SNB does not issue foreign exchange licences, approvals, or registration certificates for corporate current-account or capital-account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility. The Swiss franc (CHF) is a freely floating, freely convertible currency under both current and capital account OECD liberalisation principles and Swiss constitutional guarantees on free movement of capital. There is no exchange control statute, no prior notification or approval requirement for purchasing or selling foreign currency, no restriction on maintaining foreign-currency accounts in Switzerland, and no limitation on dividend, profit, interest, or liquidation proceeds remittance from a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft to non-resident shareholders. The only friction is the ordinary Swiss anticipatory withholding tax of 35% on dividends, which is reduced or refunded under applicable double tax treaties, and there is no requirement to repatriate trade receivables, no mandatory hedging rule, and no license gate for FDI inflows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, no fixed repatriation timeline, and no duty to deposit export earnings with the SNB for used hydraulic excavators, rollers, or any other exported goods. Export proceeds in USD, EUR, or other currencies may be retained indefinitely in Swiss or foreign banks. The only passive reporting duties are: (i) SNB statistical balance-of-payments surveys for enterprises with quarterly cross-border transaction volume above the CHF 1.5 million reporting threshold; (ii) customs export value declarations in the TARES/NCTS process administered by the Federal Customs Administration; (iii) AMLA cash transaction reporting for cash movements exceeding CHF 10,000; and (iv) SECO embargo compliance, notably the prohibition on trade and receivable collection involving sanctioned Russian or Belarusian counterparties in the construction machinery sector.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account 'Sperrkonto' for the AG's liberating share capital; multi-currency corporate operational account (CHF, EUR, USD); documentary letter of credit issuance, advising and negotiation account; treasury and FX settlement window.
Capital escrow sub-account evidencing the CHF 100,000 share capital deposit; CHF operating current account; EUR and USD pass-through nostro facilities; SNB statistical reporting assistance.
Commercial current account in CHF and EUR; documentary collections and standby letters of credit; trade finance guarantee collateral window.
CHF operating and treasury account; SME working capital credit lines; limited documentary collection infrastructure through the cooperative banking network.
CHF payment and merchant settlement account for domestic cash-side automation; no in-house documentary LC capability and no specialised used-machinery trade compliance desk.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury rail, Medium as a supplementary payment conduit. A FINMA-authorised FinTech licence holder under Article 1b of the Swiss Banking Act, or an EU/EEA PSD2 electronic money institution (e.g. Airwallex, Revolut Business), may be used for low-value incidental payment traffic, but such providers cannot issue SWIFT documentary letters of credit, do not provide a bankable capital-deposit confirmation acceptable to Swiss notaries, and generally lack the correspondent banking depth required for six-to-seven-figure used construction equipment settlements. Offshore EMIs also create AML friction: Swiss banks apply enhanced due diligence where corporate funds cycle through non-regulated payment intermediaries, and several first-tier Swiss banks impose contractual prohibitions on routing concentration of trade inflows through EMI wrappers. The compliant architecture is a fully licensed Swiss bank as principal treasury and clearing anchor, with any EMI layer restricted to lightweight operational micropayments and expressly disclosed in the KYC file.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory in practice for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced corporate client. Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA) and the banks' self-regulatory Due Diligence Agreement (VSB/CDB 2020), Swiss banks require at least one director with authorised signatory power to appear in person at a bank branch, or before a certified notary or external counsel acting on the bank's mandate, for the identity verification and beneficial-ownership interview. Video identification is accepted for selected low-risk retail and simple corporate onboarding, but for an import-export AG trading used excavators with cross-border counterparties and sanctions-sensitive geographies, remote-only onboarding is normally unavailable. The KYC file must include: original or notarially certified passport of the director, residence permit if non-Swiss, board resolution naming account signatories, a Swiss Commercial Register extract not older than 30 days, and signed AMLA/UBO forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flag: used excavator invoice value mismatches, over- or under-invoicing against market benchmarks, frequent revised invoices, or price decoupling between the sale contract, customs declarations, and transport documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial defence file: (i) fully executed sale and purchase agreement with HS 8429 classification, INCO terms, exact equipment serial numbers/chassis/VIN, year of manufacture and engine hours; (ii) independent pre-shipment inspection certificate from SGS, Bureau Veritas or a neutral surveyor; (iii) valuation benchmarks from two public used-equipment platforms (Ritchie Bros, MachineryTrader) confirming the commercial plausibility of the charged price; (iv) bill of lading or CMR with container and seal numbers; (v) export or import customs declarations; (vi) transport insurance certificate tracing the route; and (vii) chronological payment evidence demonstrating no circular rebate or round-tripping.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unresolved beneficial ownership: indirect shareholding through foreign intermediary companies, bearer share legacy structures, nominee directors, or layered trusts triggering the UBO-refresh procedure under AMLA Articles 4 and 6.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle: (i) certified Swiss Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) dated within 30 days; (ii) signed UBO declaration disclosing all natural persons holding more than 10% of the share capital or voting rights; (iii) certified identification documents of the ultimate beneficial owners; (iv) opening balance sheet certified by a Swiss fiduciary or, where available, audited annual financial statements of the AG; (v) corporate extract of the foreign shareholder from its home commercial register; (vi) tax-residency certificate of the foreign shareholder; and (vii) five-year personal and corporate tax filings of the beneficial owner evidencing the lawful accumulation of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo proximity: counterparties domiciled in high-risk territories (Russian Federation, Belarus, certain CIS corridors), routes crossing EU high-risk jurisdictions, or payment chains involving intermediary banks without bankable compliance reputations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance bundle: (i) automated sanctions screening log against OFAC, EU, UN, SECO and FINMA advisories with documented no-hit or false-positive resolution; (ii) end-user certificate and no-re-export undertaking from each buyer; (iii) dual-use classification memorandum confirming that secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers are not military-use items but screening nevertheless documents SECO adherence; (iv) complete payment chain showing no bank intermediary in embargoed jurisdictions; (v) PEP check on all shareholders, directors, and counterparties; (vi) declared freight route and customs officer confirmation; and (vii) board letter warranting that no sanctioned person acts as beneficial owner, supplier, buyer, freight forwarder or consignee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity: capital injection or operating deposits originating from crypto-asset exchanges, non-regulated payment service providers, or shell-account structures that trigger the enhanced-due-diligence refusal ground.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Flow-of-funds file: (i) founding shareholder's bank statement from a licensed bank confirming the origin of the CHF 100,000 statutory capital deposit; (ii) capital formation protocol and board resolution referencing the contribution as liberation of share capital under the Swiss Code of Obligations; (iii) where crypto-originated wealth is legitimate, a FINMA-authorised crypto-bank statement (e.g. Sygnum or SEBA) evidencing the fiat conversion chain; (iv) projected cash-flow forecast mapping the used-machinery trade cycle; (v) signed off-take contracts or purchase orders with credible trading counterparties; (vi) back-to-back invoice matrix aligning each inward remittance to a specific receivable; and (vii) explicit disclaimer of third-party payment routing. If residual risk persists, the treasury may pre-fund the account through a Swiss notary or fiduciary escrow pending full clearance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant capital injection protocol for the Swiss AG is as follows: (1) the board of directors resolves the capital formation and designates the receiving bank; (2) the AG opens a dedicated capital escrow sub-account, commonly known as the Sperrkonto, at the chosen Tier-1 Swiss bank; (3) the shareholder wires the statutory liberating fraction of the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital from a personal account at a licensed bank, never from a non-regulated PSP or cash-accepting intermediary; (4) the incoming SWIFT MT103 must carry an explicit purpose designation in field 70, using ISO 20022 purpose code 'CASH' or clear wording such as 'Liberierung Aktienkapital / contribution to share capital of CH_AG'; (5) the bank performs the AMLA Article 6 source-of-funds review, sanctions screens the remitter, and thereafter issues the formal paid-up capital confirmation (Bankbestätigung) attached to the notarised incorporation deed; (6) the notary files the capital evidence with the Swiss Commercial Register; (7) only after registration may the escrow account be reclassified as a free operational account. For subsequent shareholder loans, the AG must execute a written loan agreement, apply an arm's length interest rate consistent with Swiss tax practice, and report the liability to the cantonal tax authority to prevent recharacterisation as hidden equity; no interest deduction is available on disguised equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails for used excavator trading: (i) open-account settlements and pre-payments via SWIFT MT103 with UETR tracking, beneficiary sanctions pre-screening, and invoice matching; (ii) SEPA Credit Transfers in EUR for low and medium-value payments to European counterparties holding SEPA IBANs; (iii) documentary collections (CAD/DP) via SWIFT MT400/MT410 for control of title against payment in high-value export contracts with EM counterparties; (iv) commercial letters of credit issued by the Swiss bank under SWIFT MT700/MT710 pursuant to UCP 600, with transport and commercial documents checked against L/C terms, suitable for sales to Central Asian and Middle Eastern construction companies; (v) Bank Payment Obligations (BPO) under the ISO 20022 trade services utility for open-account corridors where both counterparties are onboarded; and (vi) supplier disbursements to auction houses and OEM spare-part vendors via MT103 with tax-invoice matching and correct INCO clause references. Settlement in restricted emerging currencies should be avoided; USD and EUR are the preferred settlement currencies for equipment sourced from Japanese, EU, or North American auctions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla OTC FX forwards in CHF/EUR and CHF/USD under an ISDA 2002 or Swiss Master Agreement, with tenors up to 12 months for trade-payment certainty
OTC FX swaps (swap-in and swap-out) allowing short-term rolling of export proceeds between CHF and hard currencies without exposing the AG to long-dated risk
Cross-currency swaps (CIRS) converting trade-finance interest and principal liabilities between CHF, EUR, and USD to match the underlying equipment purchase and sale cash flows

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in liquid emerging-market currencies (offshore CNY, KZT, UZS, NGN, EGP, TRY) executed through the Swiss bank's global trading desk, subject to bankability and market depth
OTC vanilla FX options (calls and puts) and zero-cost collar structures hedging the CHF profit margin on committed US-dollar or euro-denominated excavator sale contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements and management report by shareholders at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the Annual General Meeting; final approved statements retained in the corporate records and submitted to the Cantonal Tax Administration upon assessment request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months from the balance-sheet date (Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 958); for a 31 December year-end, approval must be completed no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director liability for breach of statutory duties, administrative warnings and fines up to CHF 100,000 by the Commercial Register Office, and petition-based judicial dissolution at the request of any shareholder or creditor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss corporate income tax return covering Federal Direct Tax and cantonal/municipal profit taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration for the registered seat, acting as the collecting body for federal, cantonal and municipal profit taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers; most cantons grant an automatic non-penalized extension to 30 June, and additional extensions are available at the tax administration's discretion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 3-5% per annum, late-filing fines, assessment based on available records at the tax administration's discretion, debt-execution proceedings, and continued failure may result in compulsory strike-off of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual or quarterly VAT return and corresponding payment where Swiss VAT registration is compulsory or elective
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration, Main Division VAT (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an annual VAT reporting basis, filing and payment are required within 60 days after the end of the year; for quarterly reporting, within 60 days after the end of each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment default interest, reminder fees, administrative fines of up to CHF 8,000, and in the case of tax evasion an additional sum of 3-5 times the amount of tax evaded

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social security wage declaration and employer contribution statement under the Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance (AHV/IV/EO/ALV) system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Responsible Cantonal Compensation Office (e.g., SVA) for AHV/IV/EO contributions; SUVA for mandatory occupational accident insurance declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual AHV wage declaration must be filed by 31 January of the year following the compensation year; employer contributions must be paid at each payroll date with a final annual equalization by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default interest, administrative fines up to CHF 5,000, debt enforcement proceedings, provisional assessment of contributions by compensation office, and personal director liability for unpaid employer contributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements (ordinary or limited audit) together with the auditor's report when audit is not validly waived
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders at the Annual General Meeting; the audit report is retained in the corporate records and produced to the Cantonal Tax Administration with the tax return when audited accounts are used
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit body is appointed at the prior annual general meeting; the audit must be completed and the report submitted to the board and shareholders prior to the current annual general meeting, ordinarily 3-6 months after the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a statutory auditor results in a warning from the Commercial Register Office, followed by administrative fines and possible compulsory dissolution; directors may also incur personal liability for audit-related damages

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full statutory audit is required when a Swiss AG exceeds two of the three following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above CHF 20 million, revenue above CHF 40 million, or 250 or more full-time employees. Below those thresholds, a limited audit is required unless the company has no more than 10 full-time equivalent employees and all shareholders expressly waive the audit for a one-year period; any shareholder or group holding at least 10% of share capital may nevertheless demand a limited audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963) and Swiss GAAP FER (Swiss Accounting and Reporting Recommendations); IFRS is permitted for regulated, listed, and internationally oriented companies, but all companies must keep statutory books in accordance with Swiss law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Swiss AG must maintain an up-to-date Register of Shareholders (Aktienbuch) and record any transfer of registered shares immediately; there is no separate public annual beneficial-owner filing currently in force for Switzerland. Under the pending Federal Act on Transparency of Legal Entities, once in force, each AG will be required to confirm its beneficial owners annually through a central register. In the interim, the board must ensure that the share register, director register, and minute book are continuously updated and available for inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Meetings and Board Resolutions
Audit Reports and Audit Working Papers (if audited)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-35,000 per annum depending on turnover, assets, group complexity, and audit type

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct tax (tax on profit after federal tax, equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction applies to wholesale remarketing of used construction machinery. Combined federal/cantonal/communal effective corporate income tax rate in Zug is approximately 11.9%; in higher-tax cantons it reaches approximately 21.0%. No sector-specific incentive exists for ISIC 4659 activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal corporate tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Personen), submitted via the canton's electronic tax portal (eTax für juristische Personen; in Zug, www.zg.ch/steuern); the same return cabins the Swiss federal direct tax assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline is set by the cantonal tax administration, generally 3–6 months after the close of the fiscal year. For a 31 December year-end, the return is usually due by 31 March or 30 June of the following year; extensions to 30 September or later are available upon timely request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, legal form (AG/SA), registered seat, Swiss UID/IDE/IDI number, date of incorporation, purpose and principal industry code (ISIC 4659).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG is the resident taxpayer; the non-resident shareholder's identity appears on the beneficial-owner and dividend annexes, not on the basic identification field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period, accounting year-end, and the exact dates of any short tax period or cambio of financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ownership does not alter the Swiss statutory tax period; file for the period actually used by the AG's annual financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net result per Swiss statutory annual financial statements, after book depreciation, impairment adjustments and provisions for used excavator inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare the financial statements in Swiss Francs in accordance with accounting provisions of the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 958f OR); the foreign shareholder must not consolidate into this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ziffer 20 – Non-deductible expenses / hidden profit distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses, including federal/cantonal income taxes, any hidden profit distributions, exaggerated intercompany commissions, excessive management fees and penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All transactions with non-resident shareholders or affiliates must be priced at arm's length; any adjustment made by the tax authority is added back here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ziffer 30 – Participation deduction and other reliefs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction for qualifying dividend and capital gain income from participations of at least 10% held for at least one year; plus any available cantonal reliefs (not applicable to ordinary trading).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable unless the Swiss AG holds qualifying participations; margin on used construction machinery sales is ordinary taxable trading income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of eligible losses from previous tax periods, capped at a seven-year carryforward period under DBG Art. 31.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Swiss-entity losses may be deducted; foreign parent losses are not transferable into the Swiss AG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ziffer 50 – Taxable profit and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after all corrections and loss offsets, followed by the computation of federal, cantonal and communal corporate income tax and the capital tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG must pay Swiss tax from its own assets; non-resident shareholders are not substituted for the Swiss taxpayer.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing triggers an administrative fine under DBG Art. 174 up to CHF 10,000, assessment by estimation, default interest at the annually adjusted statutory rate (currently approximately 4.25% p.a.), and possible criminal proceedings where concealment is intentional.
